title: py-sdk-streaming-record-and-replay-shim-for-deterministic-tests
creator: Evan Patel
description: Add a developer-friendly record-and-replay shim to the Python SDK streaming surface that captures streaming chat events (tokens, event types, metadata, timing) into a compact deterministic log and provides a replay harness for deterministic unit/integration tests. The shim should support both sync/async consumer patterns, optional fault injection (truncated stream, latency spikes), and hooks for telemetry to validate resume and retry semantics in CI.
acceptance_criteria: A decorator or context manager (e.g., @replayable_stream / replay_stream()) that can wrap existing streaming chat call sites with minimal API changes
Recorded streams are serializable to compact JSONND and can be replayed deterministically in tests without live network access
Replay supports configurable fault injection modes: drop-after-N-tokens, delayed-fragment, and out-of-order-fragments
Telemetry hooks expose per-fragment timing and a replay fingerprint that matches production traces for the same prompt
Comprehensive unit/integration tests demonstrating deterministic replay across event adapters and for both async iterators and generator-based consumers
README, quickstart test examples, and a GH PR with CI integration that runs replayed stream tests on every push
implementation_notes: Record format: newline-delimited JSON (JSONND) with fields: seq_id, event_type, payload_base64, t_offset_ms, rng_seed
Expose two modes: record (capture live stream) and playback (feed synthetic events into SDK consumer API surface)
Provide a small compatibility shim that maps recorded event_type to existing SDK event enums to minimize caller changes
Prefer non-blocking file IO and optional in-memory buffer for short-lived CI tests to avoid flakiness
Design for deterministic RNG seed capture so replay replicates any sampling behaviors used by model clients
Integrate with existing telemetry tags: sdk.trace_id, replay.run_id, and test_case_id for correlation in Grafana
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Recorded logs could leak PII or customer data - Mitigation: default record mode redacts text payloads unless explicit opt-in and includes a sanitized mode
Risk: Large recordings in long lived conversations - Mitigation: support configurable max_record_size and automatic summarization checkpointing

Risk: Replay diverges from production behavior due to runtime differences - Mitigation: capture runtime fingerprint (SDK version, Python minor, model variant) and fail replay if mismatch unless --force is passed
Risk: API surface complexity - Mitigation: provide two minimal ergonomics: decorator for simple tests and context manager for advanced scenarios
qa_plan: Unit tests for record/parse/write/read of JSONND logs
Integration tests that record a short live stream (dev model) and assert exact event sequence on replay
CI job that runs replayed tests under tox matrix (py38/py39/py310) and reports reproducibility metrics
Load test that records 1k short conversations and validates total storage and replay throughput
Manual exploratory testing with the Console trace view to compare recorded timing vs production traces
notes: Prototype discussed with PM and DX on 2026-02-22; decision to prioritize deterministic tests for SDK maintainability over building a full-fledged capture server for now
Trade-off: keeping record format simple (JSONND) increases file size vs binary formats; chosen for ease of debugging and portability
Follow-up item: upstream a small CLI tool to convert recorded JSONND -> compressed archive and back
We will not enable automatic recording in Hosted default builds; opt-in only for local/dev/CI. Add config flag: REDWOOD_SDK_RECORD_STREAMS=true
